csi_contrast_map — INTERFEROMETRY surface op

• Data kinds: zscan → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.csi_contrast_map(stack, remove_bias=True) (implementation को सीधे call करना हो तो import interferometry; interferometry.csi_contrast_map(stack, remove_bias=True), registry से लेना हो तो opsinterferometry.get("csi_contrast_map"))

उपयोग

हर pixel का peak fringe modulation — contrast (और validity) map।

> नीचे का विस्तृत विवरण मूल text में है — सारांश और headings का अनुवाद हो चुका है।

The maximum of each pixel's coherence envelope. Three uses, in order of how often they matter:

1. Validity. A pixel that never produced fringes — a hole, a steeply tilted facet that threw the light out of the aperture, a saturated or dark pixel — has near-zero modulation. This is the map you threshold to decide which heights from csi_height_map to trust.

2. Reflectance. In the forward model the envelope peak is exactly amplitude * reflectivity, so with a known *amplitude* this map *is* the reflectivity. Verified in the tests: a known reflectivity map over a 5.0-7.0 um surface is recovered with a maximum error of 7.32e-05 (the residual is envelope truncation again — the same surface spread over 2.0-10.0 um gives 4.03e-04). It is a contrast map, not a photometric measurement, and it is accurate to about four decimal places, not to machine precision.

3. Focus. It is the interferometric analogue of a focus measure, and it peaks where csi_height_map says the surface is.

Why use 1 rather than trust the height map everywhere: measured on a flat surface at 6.0 um with a 50x reflectance step across the field (0.02 on one half, 1.0 on the other) and 1 % noise, the "gaussian" height error is 0.146 um RMS on the bright half and 3.03 um RMS on the dark half, and 30 % of the dark pixels are refused outright. The bias barely moves (+0.14 um); what explodes is the scatter, because the three-point fit is reading three samples out of a noise floor. "centroid" degrades far more gracefully on the same data (0.022 -> 0.157 um, 7x rather than 20x), which is the second place in this module where the estimator ranking depends on the data rather than on the algebra. This map is what separates the two populations: it reads 0.035 +- 0.004 on the dark half and 0.412 +- 0.007 on the bright one.

It is deliberately not normalised by the pedestal. The classical fringe *visibility* is b/a, and computing it would need the pedestal, which remove_bias has just thrown away; returning b and saying so is honest, whereas returning b and calling it visibility would not be. Divide by numpy.mean of the stack along axis 0 if you want the ratio.

Returns a float64 (H, W) map. Same shape and validation as csi_height_map.

Raises ValueError: a non-3-D stack, fewer than 3 planes, an empty spatial extent, a stack over MAX_STACK_ELEMENTS, a non-finite / complex / masked stack, or a non-bool *remove_bias*.
